summary_paragraph: The patient, a man with a history of end-stage renal disease, diabetes, congestive heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and polysubstance use, was admitted for melena, weakness, and shortness of breath. He had a hemoglobin of 7 g/dL, consistent with acute blood loss anemia, and received two units of packed red blood cells with improvement. He was found to have hyperkalemia, managed with kayexalate and hemodialysis. A chest X-ray showed worsening pulmonary edema and pleural effusions, attributed to fluid overload. He underwent successful balloon angioplasty of his AV fistula due to stenosis. His atrial fibrillation was well rate-controlled on labetalol, and mild troponin elevation was attributed to demand ischemia. He remained stable, with no further bleeding, and was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to resume dialysis and follow up with his providers.
